reason: The F-centered orthorhombic cell (about 13.640 x 7.181 x 7.067 A) and a chemically plausible Z=4 are strongly supported by peak positions, but exact structure recovery is not established. The comparable-Rwp report is unavailable, and the trajectory never performed a validated whole-pattern refinement: it fitted extracted/grouped stick intensities with an ad hoc residual, while charge flipping failed to converge (Rcf roughly 47-57%). All submitted models show major intensity errors. For example, the selected CIF calculates the 36.30-degree line as strongest and the 36.59-degree line at only about 6% relative intensity, whereas the observed values are about 59% and 75%, with the observed maximum instead at 35.62 degrees; an independent Gaussian-profile check likewise left very large normalized residuals for every candidate. Chemistry is also weak: the selected model leaves Sc only three O neighbors within 2.4 A, alternative-1 has a 1.55 A Mg-O contact and Mg sites with only one or three such O neighbors, and alternative-2 has an Mg site with no O within 2.4 A plus a 1.75 A O-O contact. The F extinctions support the lattice, not Fmm2 versus Fmmm, the coordinates, or Mg/Sc/Cu ordering. The trace found many competing Wyckoff schemes but materialized only three convenient realizations and explicitly acknowledged unresolved ordering; lower-symmetry/order-distinct frameworks were not exhaustively instantiated or compared. A materially different, chemically constrained solution could plausibly improve the candidate set, so another attempt is warranted.
